items.tx:
Abdul El-Sayed was five years old when he asked his grandfather Jan Johnson a question.

“Grandpa, how are you my grandpa?”

His grandparents-Jan and Judy had helped raise Abdul in Michigan, and until then Abdul had never had much reason to think about how they were related. But he had begun to notice that he looked nothing like either of them.

Abdul was 3 when his parents divorced. His father, Mohamed, later married Jackie Johnson, who helped raise him. Abdul called her Mom. So when he asked Jan how he could be his grandpa, Jan gave him a simple answer. Jackie was Jan’s daughter, and Jackie was Abdul’s mom. Then Jan added, “And because I love you.”

When Abdul was older, he spent summers with his father’s family in Alexandria, Egypt. His grandmother there was Soad. She cooked over a small burner with one pot, and Abdul loved to listen to her tell stories. At the end of the summer, he would go back to Michigan, to a cottage on a lake that had been in Jackie’s family for generations. He remembers trying to explain Soad to Grandma Judy. Even now, he says, it is hard to imagine either of his grandmothers knowing what to make of the other’s life.

Soad never got to go to school. She had eight children, and two of them died before their first birthdays. When Abdul talked about her as an adult, he still counted those two babies as the aunt and uncle he would have had. Soad used to remind him that he and his cousins in Egypt were no different from one another. He had simply been given chances they had not . As such, she expected him to do something with those opportunities.

Abdul thought about Soad years later when he began looking at how long people lived. By his reckoning, there was a gap of about ten years in life expectancy between the part of Michigan where he grew up and Egypt. But what bothered him was that he could find a gap about as large much closer to home. He could get on the freeway in suburban Oakland County, drive south into Detroit and see it in less than half an hour.

After medical school, Abdul took on the job of rebuilding Detroit’s health department.

Isitoshe, 

When Abdul ran for the U.S. Senate, Jan and Judy sat together in front of a camera. They told Michigan voters that they had helped raise him. Jan talked about how Abdul had helped children get eyeglasses through his work in public health. Then he mentioned something from their own life that had never been on the news. Their grandson still bought their groceries every week.

On Tuesday, Michigan elected Abdul El-Sayed to the United States Senate. When he takes office, he will be the first Muslim ever to serve in the chamber.

Patriots,

On November 3rd, 2026, the leftists took Texas in a wave election that swept the country, the consequences of which will last generations.

First, it is important to recognize my perfect wife, Mary Catherine, my partner in 39 years of blissful marriage, our five children, and our 12 grandchildren. I thank the leanest, hardest-working campaign team in Texas politics. I am so incredibly humbled by the millions of Texans who supported this campaign and believed in me. My work is for them. We won a crushing landslide in the primary and worked nonstop every single day since. I personally spent millions of dollars on this campaign, a huge percentage of a net worth that took over 40 years of hard work and sacrifice to accumulate.

Don't shed a tear for Don Huffines. I had a great life before this campaign, and I will have a great life after it. I am not sad for myself, and I am not losing any sleep over an election. I am sad for the Texans who do not want to be slaves to their government. They just want to live their lives in freedom, knowing their leaders are strong and courageous.

I am extremely humbled and honored to have served as Texas Comptroller, because of your support and the appointment by Governor Abbott. On August 1, 2026, I was sworn in, rejected all pay and benefits, and went straight to work bringing a private-sector mindset and incredible sense of urgency to Texas government. A full list of the Huffines Administration's accomplishments will be shared at the end of my term, as there is still much to come.

For two years, at more than 500 events in every corner of this state, I warned that when Texas goes, so goes the nation. I campaigned on a simple message: 'AUDIT government. EXPOSE corruption. It's YOUR money.' I could not wait to clean out the garage, because I knew that if Republicans did not clean it out ourselves, the Democrats would use it to flip Texas blue. It turns out we were already out of time. Texas is the foundation of the national Republican Party, and now the foundation is broken.

What the Huffines Administration accomplished in the first 100 days is unprecedented, and it barely scratched the surface of what I had planned. I inherited an incomprehensible mess. Sadly, the agency had not been touched since the 1990s: rife with fraud, waste, and abuse, and leaderless. Frankly, besides the reforms we made, the Democrats will find this agency and every other state agency exactly how they left them decades ago. And that tells you why Republicans lost Texas.

The leftists will continue to grow government, drive up the cost of living, and rebuild the government school monopoly, chaining Texas families to failing schools with no way out. And of course, they will continue to whittle away at our virtue by replacing God with government.

In Texas, you never really own your home or your land. You rent your property from the government, and the rent goes up every year. The administrative state grew unchecked, and fraud, waste, and corruption went unpunished.

🚨 MORE ELECTION CONCERNS OUT OF MICHIGAN! THIS TIME IN REDFORD! 🚨

And the reports just keep coming!

A voter in Redford, Michigan, District 12, shared this video from Election Day showing what appears to be an open or malfunctioning ballot tabulation machine at his polling location.

According to the individual, he had already filled out his ballot and was attempting to scan it when he encountered this situation. He also claims that this was the ONLY ballot-scanning machine in the entire building!

Now, think about that for a second. If this was the only machine available, what procedures were being followed to ensure every ballot was properly secured, accounted for, and ultimately counted?

We’ve been discussing the growing number of election irregularities and concerning reports coming out of both Texas and Michigan following Tuesday’s midterm elections. From questions surrounding voting totals and statistical anomalies to reports of ballot-processing problems, there are legitimate questions that deserve answers.

Does this video prove election fraud? No. But it absolutely raises questions about equipment reliability, ballot security, and what happened to the ballots while this machine was being worked on.

Election officials need to explain exactly what happened, whether any ballots were affected, and how they were accounted for.

Americans deserve transparency in their elections, regardless of which political party wins!

🇺🇸 KEEP DOCUMENTING EVERYTHING!

I am currently in Scotland visiting my mother, and today I went for a haircut at Westend Hair in Glasgow.

I mentioned to the man cutting my hair that I was visiting from Israel. He immediately asked whether I was worried about Israel, given that it had, in his words, alienated the entire world.

He also claimed that the attack at Bondi would never have happened without the war in Gaza, and responded to Jew-hate with the equivalent of “all lives matter”.

I shut down the conversation, but it was an extremely uncomfortable and depressing experience. What made it worse was that he was in the middle of cutting my hair. I couldn't simply get up and leave. 

I am so utterly sick of non-Jews presuming to tell Jews what Jew-hate is, what causes it and how we should understand our own experiences. The confidence with which some people dismiss Jewish experiences while insisting that their own understanding is more legitimate is astonishing.

I could not be more glad that I made Aliyah. Experiences like this remind me why I am so happy to call Israel home.

Shabbat Shalom. May we all find some peace this Shabbat.

items.tx:
Mississippi U.S. Senate Race Update

Since Hinds County has not reported votes tonight tonight, I wouldn't expect a call in Mississippi's Senate race from VoteHub until next week at the earliest.

Colom holds a small lead, and ballots reported since Election Day have been more favorable to him than the initial returns in each county. That suggests his lead is much more likely to grow than shrink. Hinds County, a heavily Democratic county that includes Jackson, also accounts for a disproportionate share of the estimated outstanding ballots, which should help him.

The challenge is determining how many ballots remain statewide. Mississippi has a history of reporting substantial numbers of votes after Election Day, but it lacks a centralized system for tracking outstanding ballots like those in Arizona or California. Gathering that information requires contacting counties individually. We don't yet have enough information to rule out *with complete certainty* the possibility that a few Republican counties have enough outstanding ballots to give Hyde-Smith a path back.

VoteHub currently has 28 uncalled federal and gubernatorial races, most of which are highly, highly unlikely to change leaders. Even compared to those other races, Mississippi is not very high on the list of those we consider most likely to flip.

items.tx:
Let’s talk about Kirill Dmitriev.

Who is he, and why the hell is Putin’s sanctioned envoy being welcomed into the White House?

It’s not for peace talks. 

Dmitriev isn’t a career diplomat. He’s a former Goldman Sachs banker who has run Russia’s sovereign wealth fund, the Russian Direct Investment Fund, since 2011. He is a close Putin associate and was appointed Putin’s special presidential envoy for international investment and economic cooperation in 2025. The US Treasury sanctioned him and his investment fund in February 2022, explicitly identifying him as a close Putin ally and describing the fund as an instrument of Putin’s inner circle.

He’s been building financial relationships with Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar and China. He’s also been a recurring back-channel contact with Trump’s inner circle. In 2017, he sought access to Trump’s incoming administration. His reconciliation proposal reached Jared Kushner through intermediaries. He also met Erik Prince in the Seychelles. This is documented in the Mueller investigation.

In 2020, reporting revealed that Kushner maintained a private communications channel with Dmitriev. They discussed investment opportunities, international negotiations and even the Russian-funded ventilator shipment to New York.

In 2025 and 2026, Dmitriev became a central figure in Trump’s negotiations with Putin over Ukraine. He’s also been pushing for sanctions relief for Russia’s investment fund. And now he’s back in Washington, welcomed into the White House, where Trump met with him privately.

There’s another part of this story that deserves scrutiny.

The White House is giving Melania Trump considerable credit for the Oleshky ceasefire. But Pope Leo had already been working on this humanitarian crisis. He personally called Putin on October 16 to request a ceasefire, humanitarian assistance and safe evacuation. He spoke with Zelenskyy three days later. Cardinal Zuppi had been pressing the issue for weeks.

The Vatican’s diplomatic intervention is documented. The precise extent of Melania’s subsequent negotiating role has not been independently explained. And somehow, the central figure at the White House celebration is Putin’s sanctioned economic and diplomatic envoy.

Why is he here?

What is he negotiating? What is he offering? What is Putin expecting in return? And why is the American president privately meeting with Putin’s representative while Ukrainian officials are left out?

This man isn’t here simply to celebrate a humanitarian evacuation. He’s here representing Putin’s economic and political interests.

Americans deserve to know what is being negotiated in our name.

items.tx:
Cyprus has begun forcibly returning Syrian nationals whose asylum applications were definitively rejected, becoming one of the few European Union countries carrying out compulsory returns to Syria.

Deputy Migration Minister Nicholas Ioannides confirmed on November 3 that the first deportations had taken place in cooperation with Cypriot police and other government agencies.

More than 5,000 Syrian asylum applications have been rejected since December 2024, while approximately 6,000 Syrians have already returned voluntarily and another 6,000 have expressed their intention to leave.

Cypriot authorities are also accelerating the rejection of unfounded asylum applications and withdrawing subsidiary protection from individuals who no longer qualify.

The government previously introduced financial incentives for voluntary returns, including €2,000 per adult and €1,000 per child under a program launched in 2025.

Ioannides announced that inspections targeting illegal residence and undeclared employment will intensify in the coming months, with employers and landlords urged to cooperate with authorities.
